quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Are funeral procession escort vehicles classified as emergency vehicles?

options.text: Yes, they are classified as emergency vehicles.
No, they are not considered emergency vehicles.
Yes, but only when escorted by a police vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they are classified as emergency vehicles.
questions.explanation: Funeral procession escort vehicles are classified as emergency vehicles. You must yield to them when they display proper lights or sirens.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic signal ahead.
Fire station ahead.
T intersection ahead.
Left turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts you to an upcoming traffic signal. Be ready to stop for a red light or yellow light, and watch for cross traffic.

questions.question: You are parked uphill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking uphill or downhill on a road with no curb, turn your wheels so the car will roll away from the road's center if the brakes fail.

questions.question: How should you check your vehicle's blind spots when changing lanes?

options.text: Only check the left outside mirror.
Look over your left or right shoulder.
Only check the inside rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn and look over the appropriate shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: How should you prevent hydroplaning in rain?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Slow down.
Move to the road's shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down in the rain to prevent hydroplaning. Driving too fast causes your tires to ride on water instead of the road, making your vehicle hard to control.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass if you are on the side with the solid yellow line.
No one can pass from either direction.
You can pass if you are on the side with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass if you are on the side with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. When they are together, only the side with the broken line can pass safely.

questions.question: What is the safest way to back up your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn right before putting the car in reverse.
Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
Use your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.
Turn up the radio before backing up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: Walk to the back of your vehicle before driving it. Look for children and small objects that you might not see from the driver's seat.

questions.question: What color are warning signs for pedestrians, bicycles, playgrounds, schools, and school buses?

options.text: Blue
White
Brown
Yellow-green

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow-green
questions.explanation: Yellow-green signs warn about pedestrians, bicycles, playgrounds, schools, and school buses. Watch carefully for people and children near these signs.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Allow the motorcycle a full lane.
Drive on the shoulder next to the motorcycle.
Allow the motorcycle half of a lane.
Share the same lane when passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the motorcycle a full lane.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are full-size vehicles that need a complete lane to maneuver safely. Never try to share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.question: Why should you increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?

options.text: To see around the sides of the vehicle better.
Because other drivers will pull in front of large vehicles before passing.
Because following too closely traps you in the vehicle's slipstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see around the sides of the vehicle better.
questions.explanation: Truck and bus drivers cannot see vehicles directly behind them. Increase your distance behind large vehicles so you can see the road ahead and around the sides.

questions.question: You reach a four-way stop at the same time as a driver on your left. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on your left.
You do.
Whoever is signaling to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: You do.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: The best safety restraints in a car crash are:

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Only an airbag.
Both a lap and shoulder belt and an airbag.
No safety restraints.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap and shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts can double your chance of surviving a crash. Airbags work best with safety belts and provide extra protection in front-end crashes. Always wear both your shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Keep your normal speed.
Stop and look for police cars.
Let pedestrians cross first.
Go faster than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: You can turn right or left on a green light unless a sign says you cannot. When turning, you must let other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: Children up to age ____ cannot ride in the cargo area of a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Children under 18 cannot ride in the cargo area. They must sit inside the vehicle and wear a safety belt or be in a child safety seat.

questions.question: When you are in a line of traffic crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates:

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You can pass slower drivers while crossing.
Make sure your vehicle can cross completely without stopping.
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can cross completely without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before entering railroad tracks, check that you have enough room to get all the way across without stopping. Never pass other vehicles at a railroad crossing. Always check for trains before crossing the tracks.

questions.question: If you are in a minor crash with no injuries and little damage, you should:

options.text: Leave your vehicles in the traffic lane and wait for police.
Place orange traffic cones 50 and 100 feet behind the vehicles.
Move your vehicles to the shoulder of the road.
Open your trunks and hoods to signal other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicles to the shoulder of the road.
questions.explanation: Move your vehicle out of traffic and onto the shoulder as soon as possible. If your vehicle cannot be driven, police can help push it to the shoulder. Do not move anyone who is injured.

questions.question: What driving technique helps avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle.
Leave the highways quickly.
Use four-wheel drive.
Slow down and stay farther behind other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: Slow down on snow or ice. Slowing down and increasing your following distance are the best ways to avoid crashes in bad winter weather.

questions.question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track:

options.text: Wait until you can see clearly down all the tracks.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go as soon as the train passes.
Go when one track is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see clearly down all the tracks.
questions.explanation: At a multi-track crossing, do not move until you can see down all tracks. Even at a single-track crossing, wait and check again after a train passes, as another train may be coming.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Reserved parking for people with disabilities.
Slow-moving vehicle.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reserved parking for people with disabilities.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces for people with disabilities. Only vehicles with a disability license plate or disability parking placard can use these spaces.

questions.question: Drivers do not have to yield to pedestrians who are walking against the traffic light.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians, even if they are crossing against the light. Pedestrians may misjudge traffic signals.

questions.question: Why should you not use high beam headlights when driving in fog or mist?

options.text: The light reflects back into your eyes.
Oncoming vehicles cannot see you.
Vehicles behind you will follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light reflects back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, high beam headlights reflect the light back into your eyes. Use low beams instead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn left.
No left turns allowed.
No U-turns allowed.
Truck route to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turns allowed.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that left turns are not permitted.

questions.question: What speed should you always travel?

options.text: The same speed as nearby vehicles.
The posted speed limit.
A speed that fits the road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: A speed that fits the road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: You should drive at a speed that is safe for the road and weather. Never drive faster than the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a construction zone?

options.text: Stop to watch the workers.
Drive closer to the car in front of you.
Pass through carefully and do not slow down to look around.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass through carefully and do not slow down to look around.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at things in construction zones. This causes traffic to back up. Keep moving at a safe speed.

questions.question: If your turn signals do not work, what should you use to show you are turning?

options.text: Your horn
Your headlights
Hand signals
Your emergency flashers

questions.correctAnswerText: Hand signals
questions.explanation: When your turn signals are broken, use hand signals to let other drivers know you are turning.
